newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ spending to rise NZ$5 billion over three years.
newsitem.headline: NZ spending to rise NZ$5 billion over three years.

text.p: New Zealand spending will increase NZ$5 billion over three years from 1997-98 to 1999/2000 from previous budget projections, Prime Minister Jim Bolger and new Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters said on Wednesday.
More than two thirds of that sum, "considerably more than $3 billion", has been allocated to health and education.
There would also be an increase in family assistance via increases in family support and an independent tax credit
Tax cuts scheduled for 1997 would be deferred for a year to moderate any potential pressure on inflation, monetary policy or export activity.

The coalition formed on Tuesday between the conservative National Party and the nationalist New Zealand First Party agreed to "maintain a prudent approach to fiscal policy which balances additional spending in priority areas with tax
reductions and the repayment of debt".

The agreement signed by the parties on Wednesday limits additional spending to $1.2 billion in 1997-98, $1.7 billion in 1998-99, and $2.1 billion in 1999-2000 (excluding any costs from slower debt repayment).
Allocations for individual budget items will be adjusted to avoid exceeding those targets.

The projections assume the same economic growth rate as projected in Treasury's December update -- an average of 3.4 percent over three years -- while underlying inflation would average 1.3 percent in the three years to 2000.
